svg.title: Four Gates Before a Toxic-Exposure File Counts
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-pfas-file-gates; chapter number: 5; title: Four Gates Before a Toxic-Exposure File Counts; subtitle: Proof, exposure, reachability and opt-out paperwork; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Do medical records ordered across providers and years prove the injury?; pass next: G2; fail action: Hold the file; belief of exposure or a general PFAS-linked condition is not enough (Napoli Shkolnik).; gate: G2; question: Is exposure documented via firefighter work history or residency mapped by PWSID or ZIP code?; pass next: G3; fail action: Do not count the file; expect deficiency rounds (King Law has seen four).; gate: G3; question: Is client contact info current and an estate rep lined up?; pass next: G4; fail action: Chase moved and deceased claimants now; talc firms are working toward a 95% threshold and excluded clients face an uphill fight.; gate: G4; question: For Roundup opt-outs, is there an original wet signature with ID inside 90 days?; pass next: Enroll and budget at least 1.5 years to first funds; fail action: No DocuSign; a missed window sweeps the file into the class.; caption: Toxic-exposure dockets pay only after defendants can count their liability; the AFFF MDL drew 131,000 filings and was scrubbed toward 80,000 to 90,000.; assumptions note: Gate order is a sequencing of separately reported practitioner checks. Settlement lag of at least 1.5 years is Michael Stanisci's rule of thumb.; note: Sources: King Law (aOm5hBG6t9s), Napoli Shkolnik (S1VC15_WonY), Jon and Marc (NHmq2W3F_do, 3Qxw8dtCCns), Steve Smith on Cut to the Chase Network (-H3O5pPP-XA), Michael Stanisci (_qBek9AFPiI).

text.title: Four Gates Before a Toxic-Exposure File Counts
text.tspan: Four Gates Before a Toxic-Exposure File Counts

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Do medical records ordered across providers and years prove the injury?; pass next: G2; fail action: Hold the file; belief of exposure or a general PFAS-linked condition is not enough (Napoli Shkolnik).

gate: G2; question: Is exposure documented via firefighter work history or residency mapped by PWSID or ZIP code?; pass next: G3; fail action: Do not count the file; expect deficiency rounds (King Law has seen four).

gate: G3; question: Is client contact info current and an estate rep lined up?; pass next: G4; fail action: Chase moved and deceased claimants now; talc firms are working toward a 95% threshold and excluded clients face an uphill fight.

gate: G4; question: For Roundup opt-outs, is there an original wet signature with ID inside 90 days?; pass next: Enroll and budget at least 1.5 years to first funds; fail action: No DocuSign; a missed window sweeps the file into the class.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order is a sequencing of separately reported practitioner checks. Settlement lag of at least 1.5 years is Michael Stanisci's rule of thumb.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Gate order is a sequencing of separately reported practitioner checks. Settlement lag of at least 1.5 years is Michael
